name: Alan Jackson
kind: SEARCHED, NOT FOUND - no portrait exists in reach
fact: Alan Lawrence Jackson sat for no class portrait in any volume that could hold him, and the two photographs the archive does reach both hide his face. The 1980 Talisman index gives him exactly two pages, 'Jackson, Alan Lawrence 124, 423'. Printed p. 423 is a 'Student teacher' feature whose caption reads that helping kids with their social studies at McNeill Elementary School is part of sophomore Alan Jackson's contribution to tutoring efforts for his fraternity: the frame holds two elementary-school children facing the camera and one figure in the foreground with the back of the head to the lens, which is the tutor, so his face is not in the picture. Printed p. 124 is the Halloween spread, and its caption on p. 125 names five studio subjects, Molly and Betsy Bogdan, Alan Jackson, Candy Bush and Kathleen Hancock. He is the only man of the five and the p. 124 right-hand frame is the only man on the page, so the identification is sound, but the whole point of the frame is a Hallowe'en skull mask and makeup covering the face. The 1981 index lists him with no page numbers at all, so he is in no photograph in that volume. The 1982 index gives him one page, 'Jackson, Alan Lawrence 266', the Kappa Alpha Psi pledging feature 'Step in line' on pp. 266-267, where he is named twice in the body and once in a caption as the owner of the apartment the picture was taken in, and is in none of the four photographs. He was a senior that year, so the 1982 volume is his last chance at a grid cell and he is not in it. Corroboration that this is the right man and not a namesake: the 1980 caption calls him a Tampa, Fla., sophomore, the 1982 body text a Plant City, Fla., senior (two towns twenty miles apart in the same county, and the class years line up), and he is a Kappa Alpha Psi brother, which fits the Chair of Minority Affairs. Note that the 1982 caption on p. 266 calls him a Paducah senior, contradicting its own body text on the same page.

name: METHOD: archive.org 1986 and 1987 Talismans, corrected leaf arithmetic
kind: correction to a recorded offset - costs a wasted download if you get it wrong
fact: Two separate numbers, and the earlier notes conflated them. (1) PAGE IMAGES: printed page = image leaf minus 3, for BOTH 1986 and 1987. Verified against printed folios: 1987 image leaf n117 is p. 114 (the Associated Student Government spread), n365 is p. 362, n372 is p. 369, n374 is p. 371; 1986 image leaf n195 is p. 192, n373 is p. 370, n374 is p. 371, n378 is p. 375, n379 is p. 376. The same rule holds for 1980: image leaf n426 is p. 423 and n427 is p. 424. (2) OCR TEXT STREAM: the leaf number that scripts/talisman.py computes by bisecting the hOCR page index runs THREE HIGHER than the image leaf on the 1987 item. Stream leaf 120 is image leaf 117. So from a search hit, image leaf = stream leaf minus 3 and printed page = stream leaf minus 6. Fetching the page at the stream's own leaf number lands three pages late, which is what made the 1987 index look as though A ran to R.

topic: THE 1987 TALISMAN'S hOCR TEXT INDEX RUNS TEN LEAVES AHEAD OF THE PAGE IMAGES ON archive.org
note: Established on 7 September 2026 by reading the printed folio off the image, which is the only safe way. For every other archive.org Talisman the rule holds that the image is n = (1-based hOCR leaf) - 2: 1972 text leaf 409 is image n407 and is printed p. 404. On the 1987 volume it does NOT. The senior run Glenar to Hobgood, which carries Richard Helms, sits in hOCR leaf 312, and the matching image is n302, printed p. 299 - ten leaves back, not two. Image n310, which the ordinary rule would have given, is printed p. 307 and carries the Nass to Riddle run instead. The volume's own back index is the check: it reads 'Helms, Richard Eugene 137, 299', 'Helton, Gregory Wallace 139, 299', 'Hemstapat, Udomchai 118, 299' and 'Hamilton, Mark Moore 149, 299', all four of them people printed in that same block, and all four say 299. This is the same volume _archive-gaps.json already flags for making scripts/talisman.py compute a leaf three too high, so treat every 1987 page number as suspect until the folio has been read off the image. 1986 is NOT affected: image n298 is printed p. 295 by the ordinary rule and the index agrees ('Davis, Betsy 295').

topic: THE 1982-1985 TALISMANS WERE SWEPT WHOLE ON 8 SEPTEMBER 2026 - and the 1983 volume is the good one
note: All four volumes on disk at ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_topscholar-pdfs/ were opened and matched against ALL 796 people in the nine worklists. RESOLUTION IS THE WHOLE STORY HERE. The 1983 volume (two parts, dlsc_ua_records 406 and 407, 394 pages) is scanned at about 1890 by 2390 pixels a PRINTED PAGE, which is three to four times every other TopSCHOLAR Talisman of the decade and gives grid cells of 200 to 230 pixels. It has NO embedded text layer at all, which is presumably why nobody had opened it: all 394 pages were rendered at 2.2x and OCR'd with ocrmac in about four minutes, and the output is at /tmp only, so re-OCR if needed - it is quick. The 1984 and 1985 volumes store one image per two-page SPREAD at 1760 by 1216, so a printed page is 880 px and a cell about 110 by 155; their embedded text layers exist but are unusable OCR sludge, so they too were re-OCR'd. The 1982 volume's text layer is readable in places and was searched, but at 816 by 1123 a page it is the worst of the four. LEAF TO PRINTED PAGE. 1983 part 2: printed page = ZERO-BASED PDF index + 193 (PDF 126 is p. 319, PDF 164 is p. 357, both read off the folio). 1984: left page of the spread = 2 x zero-based PDF index - 6, calibrated on three neighbouring leaves (PDF 51 prints 97 bottom right, PDF 52 prints 98 bottom left, PDF 54 prints 102). GRID LAYOUTS: 1983 is SIX across with the names in one column in the outer margin in blocks of six, except the graduate-student pages which are FIVE across; 1984 is FIVE across per half-spread with the names in the outer margin in blocks of five. YIELD for this block: Laura Robb (1983 p. 319), Ronnie Bryant (1983 p. 357), James Moorman and Frank Miller (1983 p. 275) and Jorge Garcia (1984 p. 100).

topic: KELLY SMITH AND KELLY S. SMITH: the 1985 Talisman prints BOTH forms, adjacent, and a later pass can settle it with one source
note: Found 8 September 2026 and left uncut deliberately. The archive holds two separate records - Kelly Smith, On-Campus Representative 1982-83, and Kelly S. Smith, Treasurer 1983-84 - and it has never been established whether they are two women or one woman entered twice. The 1985 Talisman, PDF page 158 of 196 (dlsc_ua_records/409), carries TWO consecutive labels in the same name block of its portrait grid, in the outer right margin: 'KELLY SMITH' with no middle initial, immediately followed by 'KELLY S. SMITH'. Their neighbours in the block are JACK SMITH, KAREN SMITH above and WILLIAM SMITH below. Because the label block runs in printed order against the grid row, the two cells are adjacent and their order is fixed, so IF the archive's two records are these two women the mapping is unambiguous and both faces can be cut in one go. What is missing is any source giving a middle name for either, and both are women, so the sex check that proves every other row in this file cannot separate them. THIS IS ALSO THE ANSWER TO THE 1980 AND 1981 GRIDS, where the only Kelly Smith is KELLY J. SMITH of Louisville, management, Bowling Green - a THIRD person, and the reason those two volumes were correctly rejected. Anyone finding a middle name or hometown for either officer should come straight back to 1985 PDF 158.

topic: CONNIE HOFFMANN (Activities Vice President 1984-85): the only photograph is of her and her twin sister, and the caption is not positional
note: Worked out fully on 8 September 2026 and left uncut. Connie Hoffmann is Cornelia Hoffmann, and the 1983 Talisman's back index carries her ONCE - 'Hoffmann, Cornelia 22' - against 'Hoffmann, Astrid 22, 244, 292' for her twin sister. Page 22 is a feature called Double dilemma about five sets of twins at Western, and it prints a two-person photograph captioned simply 'Connie and Astrid Hoffmann'. Two women, no left, no right, no other marker: this is the same objection _do-not-use.json records against the Stephen Mayer and Mark Clark photographs, and the Lodmell twins are the archive's standing warning about exactly this. WHAT A LATER PASS CAN DO. Astrid Hoffmann's own class portrait exists and is precisely located: 1983 Talisman part 2, printed p. 292, sophomore grid, six across and nine rows, ninth row and third cell, the block reading WAYNE C. HOBBS II, THOMAS E. HODGES III, ASTRID HOFFMANN, SUSAN K. HOFSASS, TERESA LYNNE HOLMAN, MONICA HOLTON against a printed row of man, man, woman, woman, woman, woman. An editor able to look at both images can decide which of the two women on p. 22 is Astrid and therefore which is Connie. That is a judgement about a face and belongs to a person, not to this pass. The text of the feature adds that they are FRATERNAL twins from Gallatin, Tennessee, sophomores in 1982-83, that Astrid is a nursing major, and that they do not live together.
